sentiment.instructions: Judge the overall sentiment the tweet's author expresses or conveys: their attitude toward what they mention, their mood, or the clear good/bad nature of reported news. Label by evaluative tone, not topic; dates, events and celebrities alone are neutral.

criteria.positive: Author clearly shows enthusiasm, liking, approval, hope, gratitude or praise (impressed, sounds perfect, love, can't wait, let's go, :) ), defends or compliments someone, or promotes/invites with upbeat wording (celebrate, win, who wants tickets, don't miss, come support, please share). Also wins the author cheers, condolences with prayers or blessings (RIP, may God bless), well-wishing.
criteria.neutral: Factual reports, wire-style news and sports results stated without cheering, event notices giving only logistics (register, RSVP, meeting at 6pm), spam, questions, requests or pleas to celebrities, hedged opinions (may be, could be, is it still...?), plans, live game commentary and player-stat remarks. Also jokes, banter and fangirl hyperbole (lol, lmao, bwahaha, I'm dead, not ready), laughing at one's own mishaps, wry corrections, and mixed feelings where positive and negative balance.
criteria.negative: Author sincerely shows displeasure: anger, sadness, disappointment, disgust, dread, boredom or contempt, including real complaints about their situation (going to die, ugh, I miss, not because I enjoy it), grumbling about products or services, sarcastic or insinuating criticism (perhaps a bit insensitive, #justsaying), pointed political/religious criticism, insults, wishing harm. Also reports of bad events: attacks, bombings, deaths, crimes, arrests, losses, scandals, injuries, failures.
